title: "A" Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit High (Bank 1)
plain: The computer is watching the "A" rocker arm position sensor (bank 1) and is reading a voltage that is higher than it should be, which often means a broken ground or a short to power. This sensor tells the computer which valve lift mode the rocker arms are actually in.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Variable valve lift may be disabled
Possible loss of power at higher rpm

causes.name: Signal wire shorted to voltage or a broken ground wire
Failed rocker arm actuator position sensor
Corroded or loose connector
Control module fault (rare)

checks: Inspect the wiring and ground connection for the "A" rocker arm position sensor (bank 1)
Check for wires melted or rubbed together in the harness
Measure the circuit with a meter before replacing parts
fix: Repair the open ground or shorted wire; if the wiring is fine, replace the rocker arm actuator position sensor.

title: "A" Rocker Arm Actuator Position Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic (Bank 1)
plain: The computer is watching the "A" rocker arm position sensor (bank 1) and is seeing a signal that cuts in and out. This sensor tells the computer which valve lift mode the rocker arms are actually in.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Variable valve lift may be disabled
Possible loss of power at higher rpm

causes.name: Loose connector or chafed wire that loses contact over bumps
Rocker arm actuator position sensor failing on and off
Corrosion inside the connector
Poor ground connection

checks: Wiggle the wiring for the "A" rocker arm position sensor (bank 1) with the engine running while watching live data
Check connector pins for corrosion or spread terminals
Note when it happens (hot, cold, bumps) to narrow it down
fix: Repair the loose or corroded connection; replace the rocker arm actuator position sensor if the wiring is solid.

title: "B" Rocker Arm Actuator Control Circuit/Open (Bank 1)
plain: The computer is watching the "B" rocker arm actuator control circuit (bank 1) and sees what looks like a broken or disconnected circuit. This oil-operated part switches the valves between low and high lift, like Honda VTEC.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Loss of power, especially at higher rpm
Rough idle or hesitation in some cases

causes.name: Unplugged, loose or corroded connector at the rocker arm oil control solenoid
Broken or chafed wire in the "B" rocker arm actuator control circuit (bank 1)
Failed rocker arm oil control solenoid
Blown fuse or failed relay feeding the circuit
Control module fault (rare)

checks: Look over the connector and wiring for the "B" rocker arm actuator control circuit (bank 1), checking for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check power, ground and resistance of the part with a meter
Clear the code and see if it comes back
fix: Repair the wiring or connector if it is damaged; otherwise replace the rocker arm oil control solenoid.

title: "B" Rocker Arm Actuator System Performance/Stuck Off (Bank 1)
plain: The "B" rocker arm actuator (bank 1) is not responding the way the computer expects. This oil-operated part switches the valves between low and high lift, like Honda VTEC.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Loss of power, especially at higher rpm
Rough idle or hesitation in some cases

causes.name: Engine oil low, dirty or the wrong thickness
Clogged oil screen or filter at the rocker arm solenoid
Sticking rocker arm oil control solenoid
Faulty oil pressure switch for the rocker system
Worn or sticking rocker arm locking pins

checks: Check the oil level and condition first
Inspect the screen or filter at the rocker solenoid for debris
Command the solenoid with a scan tool and check the oil pressure switch reading
fix: Often fixed with an oil change to the right oil plus a cleaned screen; otherwise replace the solenoid or pressure switch.

Engine may not start or may stall

Control module fault (rare)

checks: Look over the connector and wiring for the fuel shutoff valve "B" control circuit, checking for damage, corrosion or a loose fit

title: Fuel Mode Indicator Lamp Control Circuit
plain: The circuit for the dash light that shows which fuel mode the vehicle is using (for example on flex-fuel or dual-fuel systems) has a fault.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Fuel mode light may not work

causes.name: Faulty indicator lamp
Wiring or connector fault
Instrument cluster or engine computer fault

checks: Check the lamp during the key-on bulb check
Inspect the indicator wiring
fix: Repair the wiring or the indicator lamp circuit.

title: Actuator Supply Voltage "B" Circuit/Open
plain: The computer is watching the actuator supply voltage "B" circuit and sees what looks like a broken or disconnected circuit. This is a shared power feed the computer uses to run several actuators, such as solenoids and valves.
symptoms: Check engine light on
Several systems may stop working at once
Reduced power or limp mode possible

causes.name: A shorted actuator pulling the supply voltage down
Blown fuse or failed relay in the supply circuit
Wiring short or open in the supply circuit
Engine computer fault (rare)

checks: Look over the connector and wiring for the actuator supply voltage "B" circuit, checking for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check power, ground and signal with a meter
Clear the code and see if it comes back
fix: Find the shorted actuator or wire on the shared supply and repair it, then replace any blown fuse.
